notes: Identity verified from the supplied document: title Superior facial emotion recognition in adolescents with anorexia nervosa – A replication study; Anca Sfärlea, Christina Buhl, Linda Lukas, Gerd Schulte‐Körne; DOI 10.1002/erv.3103; European Eating Disorders Review 2024, 32:943–951. This is a full primary brief report (abstract, methods, results, discussion, references), not an abstract-only parse. No PDF is assigned. The Supplement is referenced but is not contained in the supplied source. The main report explicitly sends misclassification results to the Supplement, which is not supplied. The broad description also does not identify an emotion, error category or model term. No numeric target is selected. Misclassification results are explicitly located in the unavailable Supplement; no printed candidate coefficients or p values for those models in the supplied report. Candidate common main-report analytic sample: 33 AN + 41 HC = 74 adolescent participants in mutually exclusive included groups; not derived from degrees of freedom. Main report describes the mixed TASK × EMOTION × GROUP ANOVAs and no additional participant exclusions for those reported models. Eligibility excludes IQ <85, visual impairments, specified neurological/psychiatric disorders and substance abuse; HC excludes current/past mental disorders. Endnote 2 describes a separate sensitivity analysis excluding two AN participants above the 10th BMI percentile; this is not substituted for the main analysis. Model sample cannot be assigned to an unidentified row-specific test; retain only as a candidate. Misclassification model inclusion/exclusions cannot be verified without Supplement. Authors explicitly describe successful replication at whole-study level; reported_success preserves that narrative verdict only, not a claim of a uniquely identified row-specific test. The neutral description mentions major depression; the replication actually compares AN with HC, with depression sometimes comorbid within AN, not a separate major-depression group. No mapping is inferred from row order, original statistics or numeric agreement.
